newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates three sub-funds of Luxembourg SICAV AAAf.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates three sub-funds of Luxembourg SICAV AAAf.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it had assigned its AAAf bond fund rating to the three sub-funds of the Luxembourg SICAV "LUXBOND."
"LUXBOND SICAV, is composed of three different sub-funds denominated respectively in Francs, Deutschemarks (DEM) and Dollars," S&P said in a statement.

"Its main investment objective is to provide an attractive income yield on the bond markets, for each sub-fund, whilst maintaining moderate risk and a high level of liquidity," the rating agency said.

S&P said the funds' assets consisted mainly of fixed income securities denominated in Luxembourg and Belgium Francs for "LUXBOND FRANCS," and mainly DEM, Dutch Guilders and Swiss Francs for "LUXBOND D-MARK" and denominated in U.S. and Canadian Dollars for "LUXBOND DOLLARS."
"Currency risk is not hedged and derivatives would only be used for the purpose of achieving a hedge against market fluctuations," S&P said.

"Funds rated AAAf, the highest rating by Standard & Poor's, provide extremely strong protection against credit default, for the investor," the agency said. "At least, 85 percent of the securities of each LUXBOND sub-fund have AAA long-term and/or A1 plus short-term ratings."
S&P said the administrative and custodial resources at the SICAV's disposal, as well as the quality of the internal controls and supervision, reinforced the portfolio's excellent credit profile.

"The Credit Quality Rating of this fund, identified by the "f" subscript, is assigned to funds or pools which exhibit variable net asset values. The "f" subscripted rating is a current assessment of the overall credit quality of the portfolio and reflects the level of protection against loss from credit defaults," S&P said.

S&P said the rating was based mainly on research analysis of the funds' management, on the credit quality of the investment in each sub-fund, on the likelihood of counterparty default and on the risk related to the custodian.

"LUXBOND is managed by Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat, Luxembourg (rated AA plus/A1 plus by S&P) which also acts as custodian, registrar, transfer-, domiciliary- and administration agent to the SICAV," the agency said.

"LUXBOND is distributed through the branch network of three promoters, Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat, Luxembourg, Caisse Centrale Raiffeisen SC and Cerabank Luxembourg. In total, the UBAM SICAV consists of sixteen separate compartments, eight are invested in equities and eight in bonds and other fixed income securities," S&P said.
It said a rating was not requested for the eighth bond compartment.
